environment.nativeIntegration: manual Node preload only; no IntentWeave production source changes

candidate.name: ASCII full-depth dictionary scanner inside HeuristicKeywordExtractor.extractDictionary
candidate.boundary: Simple ASCII token scan only; regex terms, structured extraction, seen/addMatch, and KWX aggregation remain TypeScript.

parity.completeKeywordMatchFields: name, originalText, UTF-16 offset, length, source
normalizedForComparison: Generated _meta and conformance snapshot rows excluded
FTS index tables excluded as derived data
def_use_chains.id excluded as a surrogate row id

scannerBenchmark.dictionaryPreparation: One N-API object per document/comment input group; one text scan call per chunk

limitations: This is a manual runtime preload, not a production feature or automatic transformation.
The prepared native dictionary assumes the per-build Set is unchanged; the public extractor API permits callers to mutate that Set, so production integration must preserve that contract.
No peak RSS, allocation, or GC measurements were captured.
The full build matrix is one macOS arm64 host and one current workspace snapshot; repeat on a stable snapshot and another host before making a general speedup claim.
def_use_chains differs across TypeScript-only runs as well as native-preload runs; its current nondeterminism remains unresolved.
The CARI DB contained eight stale document rows; the benchmark used current files from IntentWeave's official discovery routine.
decision: Promising real offload kernel: exact full KeywordMatch parity and a 1.225x five-run full-build median exceed the provisional 1.2x gate narrowly. Proceed to an opt-in integration design only after RSS/GC measurement and a safe strategy for mutable dictionaries; do not enable by default or generalize to the full extractor.
